research_brief.hypothesis: A pathway cannot be classified as deployable supplementary supply unless critical readiness domains are simultaneously supported by sufficiently transferable evidence.
alternative_explanations: A biological-only evidence summary may already be adequate.
System constraints may not materially alter shortage-relief inferences.
Observed differences may be driven by conservative thresholds rather than meaningful readiness structure.
falsification_conditions: No classification differs between biological-only and gated models.
Critical-domain gating fails to identify a decision-relevant missing-evidence case.
Sensitivity findings are fully determined by unbounded assumptions.

analysis.comparison: biological-only classification versus non-compensatory gated classification
counterexamples: biological success without production quality scale
biological success without implementable infection follow-up
technical feasibility concentrated in a few high-resource centers
analysis.missing_data_rule: Unknown or non-transferable critical evidence produces MODEL_OR_EVIDENCE_ABSTAIN, not optimistic imputation.
